---
title: "How do I display and label the frequency of categories?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I display and label the frequency of categories?

## Steps to decide and solve

Identify the category column; count each category; use bars with a zero baseline, labels, and explicit frequency units.

## Worked example: iris

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("iris")
counts <- ru_apply("bar_chart", data=d, x="Species")
stopifnot(sum(counts)==nrow(d))
```

The three flower species occur equally often in the provided Iris dataset. Bar charts compare categories; they do not imply species labels lie on a continuous axis.

## Apply it to another question

```r
ru_apply("bar_chart", data=your_data, x="category_column")
```

If you have pre-aggregated counts instead of one category per row, keep the frequencies as weights rather than treating every summary row as one occurrence.

Use `ru_plan("bar_chart")` to inspect alternative routes when required information is absent or uncertain.
